newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir suddenly delays docking after computer failure.
newsitem.headline: Mir suddenly delays docking after computer failure.

text.p: The crew aboard the ailing Mir space station abruptly postponed a planned docking with its Progress cargo resupply ship on Sunday after a computer failure, a top Mission Control official said.
"The computer aboard the Progress failed to work about three hours before the redocking," Viktor Blagov, deputy flight director at Mission Control, told Reuters.
Mir's redocking with the seven-metre (23 feet) long Progress had been scheduled to take place at 5.54 p.m. Moscow time (1354 GMT).
"There is no danger. We are now studying the situation and are planning this procedure for tomorrow," Blagov said. The Progress "is quite far from the ship," he added.

The manoeuvre was to repeat a procedure carried out on June 25 when a different Progress vehicle docking with Mir collided into the station's Spektr module, causing a major loss of power in the worst accident of the space station's 11-year history.
On Sunday, however, the Mir crew of two Russians and one British-American had planned to attempt the docking in automatic rather than manual pilot as in June.
"Its computer is always off and two or three hours before a redocking we turn it back on when it is on autopilot to make the docking. But it just didn't turn on," Blagov said.
"We'll study it now to figure out why, and if we can understand why, we'll repeat the procedure tomorrow," he said.
The latest Progress problem is likely to delay plans again to repair the Spektr module, which was punctured in the June accident, Blagov said.
The crew had planned to reattach cables into the Spektr on Wednesday to restore power in the space station.
"It will be somewhat delayed, by one day," Blagov said. He added the exact rescheduling would become clear on Monday.
